newsitem.title: USA: Arafat says "no alternative" to peace with Israel.
newsitem.headline: Arafat says "no alternative" to peace with Israel.

text.p: Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat said on Tuesday he has "no other alternative" but to press peace negotiations with Israel despite Israel's decision to build new Jewish housing in East Jerusalem.

"It is our duty and our job and our target to carry on with the peace process," Arafat said in a speech at the National Press Club. "We have no other alternative. And in spite of all the difficulties we are facing, we have one alternative: to carry on with the peace process. This is our strategic target."

Arafat, who received support from U.S. President Bill Clinton on the Jerusalem settlements issue during White House talks on Monday, repeated Arab condemnation of Israel's decision to build 6,500 new homes for Jews in predominantly Arab East Jerusalem. Israel has occupied the city since the 1967 war.

"What has been declared recently by the Israeli government has made very difficult circumstances for the peace process," said Arafat, who waived aside an interpreter and spoke in halting English. "It is a real challenge for the peace process. No one can imagine the damage for the peace process for that (housing) decision."
"It will isolate Jerusalem more and more and more and more and ... separate between Jerusalem and Bethlehem."

Arafat was rounding out a two-day visit to the United States, which has led efforts to mediate Middle East peace. He called his talks with Clinton "very constructive, positive, warm," and noted that the president had also criticised the East Jerusalem housing decision. "I haven't the right to say what he is going to do, but I'm sure he will push forward with all his capability to save the peace process," Arafat said.
